clue.text: Girl having a short walk

indicators.note: something short has been cut, so the walking word loses its final letter

parts.note: a stride is a long step in walking

explanation.surface: A young woman setting off on a quick stroll.
explanation.definitionFit: Astrid is a female first name, so it fits a girl in crossword terms.

clue.text: Animal from mountain, a cat with no tail

indicators.note: losing its tail means the last letter of the feline word is dropped

parts.note: an Alp is a high mountain

explanation.surface: A creature on a mountainside: a cat that has lost its tail.
explanation.definitionFit: The alpaca is a South American mammal related to the llama, bred for its wool.

clue.text: First-class crumble and pie over in restaurant

indicators.note: turned over means everything before it is read from the other end

parts.note: A1 means first-class, with the 1 written as the letter I
to crumble is to rot or decay

explanation.surface: Crumble and pie on the menu at a fine Italian eatery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crumble' and 'pie' look like desserts, but crumble is a verb meaning decay. AI + ROT + TART read backwards gives TRAT-TOR-IA.
explanation.definitionFit: A trattoria is an informal Italian restaurant.

clue.text: I do it foolishly, being a fool!

indicators.note: doing something foolishly suggests the letters are jumbled carelessly

explanation.surface: Someone admitting they act stupidly and so are a fool.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiot is a stupid person, a synonym for fool.

clue.text: Knight's weapon, auction item

parts.note: a lance is a long spear used by mounted knights
each item sold at auction is a lot

explanation.surface: A knight's spear going under the hammer at auction.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'is', joining the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Lancelot is the best-known knight of King Arthur's Round Table.

clue.text: FIFA's president, for example, is in an advantageous position

definitions.meaning: read literally: a head of football, the game
the idiom for being in front of rivals

explanation.surface: Football's top official is well placed.
explanation.walkthrough: The first reading splits the phrase literally: football's president is one head of 'the game'.
explanation.definitionFit: Being ahead of the game is an idiom for being better informed or prepared than competitors.

clue.text: Return with pardon?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to visit once more
second meaning: a request to repeat what was said

explanation.surface: Coming back carrying a request to hear something again.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means both to revisit a place and, as a question, asking someone to repeat themselves.

clue.text: Member's introduction to old dance

parts.note: an arm or leg is a member of the body

indicators.note: an introduction is the opening, so only the first letter of the next word is used

explanation.surface: A club member is introduced to some traditional dance.
explanation.definitionFit: The limbo is a Caribbean dance in which performers lean back under a lowered bar.

clue.text: Saying little, volunteers about one opportunity

parts.note: the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve force
your turn is your chance or opportunity

explanation.surface: Quiet volunteers waiting for their one chance.
explanation.definitionFit: A taciturn person is reserved and uncommunicative in speech.

clue.text: Released from nick, unfit

parts.note: freed from something is out of it
in good nick is British slang for in good condition

explanation.surface: A prisoner let out of jail is in poor shape.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nick' looks like British slang for prison, but here it means condition, as in 'in good nick'.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone out of condition lacks physical fitness.

clue.text: Cliché from first of prisoners given freedom

indicators.note: first of points to the opening letter of the next word only

explanation.surface: A tired phrase from a prison officer about letting inmates out.
explanation.definitionFit: A platitude is a trite remark used too often, much like a cliché.

clue.text: Imitate La Bohème female beginning to cry

parts.note: Mimì is the heroine of Puccini's opera La Bohème

indicators.note: a beginning is the start, so just the first letter of the following word

explanation.surface: Copy the soprano heroine of La Bohème as she starts to weep.
explanation.definitionFit: To mimic is to copy someone's manner or voice.

clue.text: Manage to score before Italian

parts.note: to score a surface is to cut a line into it
It. is the abbreviation for Italian

explanation.surface: An instruction to get a goal in ahead of the Italian player.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Score' suggests a goal, but here it means to cut a mark.
explanation.definitionFit: To cut it is informal for coping or being good enough, i.e. to succeed at a task.

clue.text: One excluded strange isle abroad

parts.note: abroad can mean out and about, away from home

explanation.surface: An outcast on a weird foreign island.
explanation.definitionFit: The odd man out is the person who does not fit and is left out of a group.

clue.text: Line in a Henry Miller novel

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a line of latitude north of the equator
second meaning: Miller's 1934 novel set in Paris

explanation.surface: Quoting a sentence from one of Henry Miller's books.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Line' looks like a line of text in the book, but it is a geographic line.
explanation.definitionFit: The tropic is a parallel of latitude at about 23 degrees north, and also the title of Miller's notorious novel.

clue.text: One who enticed children in Dieppe with rip off?

indicators.note: something gone off is spoiled or out of order, so these letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: A child-snatcher in a French port, caught in a rip-off.
explanation.definitionFit: The Pied Piper of Hamelin led the town's children away with his music.

clue.text: See pest rock violently on board single-decker

indicators.note: on board means inside a vehicle, so the jumbled letters go within the bus word
violent movement throws things about, so these letters are scrambled

parts.note: a coach is a single-deck bus

explanation.surface: A passenger spots a bug while the bus lurches about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'See' just invites the solver to look; the rearranged rock goes after the first letter of COACH.
explanation.definitionFit: The cockroach is an insect regarded as a household pest.

clue.text: Miscellaneous trades, so varied

indicators.note: something varied has been changed about, so the letters take a new order

explanation.surface: A mixed bag of jobs, all different.
explanation.definitionFit: Assorted means of various kinds, a mixture, the same as miscellaneous.

clue.text: Court trouble having fish cooked in hot Riviera resort

indicators.note: cooked means altered or doctored, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the skate is a flat fish
Nice is a resort city on the French Riviera

explanation.surface: Legal trouble for a chef serving fish in a sweltering Côte d'Azur town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Court' looks like a law court, but it is the verb: to court trouble is to invite it.
explanation.definitionFit: To skate on thin ice is an idiom for taking risks, inviting danger.

clue.text: New stakes in French football club

parts.note: N is the abbreviation for new
antes are the stakes put up in poker before the deal

explanation.surface: Fresh betting on a team from France.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New' looks like an anagram signal for stakes, but it just supplies its abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: FC Nantes is a professional football club based in the western French city of Nantes.

clue.text: Result of fine jump

parts.note: F is the pencil-grade abbreviation for fine

explanation.surface: The outcome of an excellent leap.
explanation.definitionFit: Offspring are children, the product or result of parents.

clue.text: Boy is missing a Swiss coin

indicators.note: missing means absent, so the letters spelling the little verb is are taken out of the name

explanation.surface: A lad has lost a coin from Switzerland.
explanation.definitionFit: The franc is the currency of Switzerland, and a franc is also a single coin.

clue.text: Operatic heroine not quite of sound mind

indicators.note: not quite complete means the final letter is lopped off

parts.note: someone of sound mind is normal

explanation.surface: An opera's leading lady is a little unhinged.
explanation.definitionFit: Norma is the title role of Bellini's opera, a druid priestess.

clue.text: Turbulent reign in African country

indicators.note: turbulent means disordered and churning, so the letters are mixed

explanation.surface: A stormy period of rule in an African state.
explanation.definitionFit: Niger is a landlocked country in West Africa.

clue.text: Heading for marina in carriage, a vagrant

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the vehicle word

parts.note: a trap is a light horse-drawn carriage

indicators.note: the heading is the top, so only the first letter of the harbour word

explanation.surface: A homeless person riding to the harbour in a carriage.
explanation.definitionFit: A tramp is a homeless wanderer, the same as a vagrant.

clue.text: A settler from abroad, I'm male with one permit

parts.note: M is the abbreviation for male

explanation.surface: A newcomer from overseas introduces himself as a man holding a permit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'With' simply joins the one and the permit.
explanation.definitionFit: An immigrant is a person who comes to settle in a foreign country.

clue.text: A guiding principle on credit is shown to be misplaced

indicators.note: misplaced things are put in the wrong positions, so the letters are reordered

explanation.surface: A rule about buying on credit turns out to be wrong-headed.
explanation.definitionFit: A doctrine is a principle or set of beliefs taught and held by a group.

clue.text: Famous composer — Her Majesty is among supporters

indicators.note: being among things puts one inside them, so one piece sits within the other

parts.note: HM is the abbreviation for Her Majesty

explanation.surface: The Queen sits among her loyal backers listening to great music.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Supporters' suggests loyal followers but means items of underwear.
explanation.definitionFit: Johannes Brahms was a celebrated nineteenth-century German composer.
